vc.configuration.title: Villager Colonies Settings
vc.configuration.category.settlements.to: Claim size, citizen limits and emerald prices for town and station upgrades.
vc.configuration.category.workers.toolti: Quarry workers before emerald crew upgrades. Every other job block has exactly one worker; add more stations to expand production or defense.
vc.configuration.category.mining.tooltip: Mine depth, tunnel layout, quarry depth and the delay between ore-vein yields.
vc.configuration.category.food.tooltip: Harvest speed and the time between regular meals. Hover a setting to see the time conversion.
vc.configuration.category.enchanting.too: How long enchanters work and the highest enchanting level they can reach.
vc.configuration.category.defense.toolti: Alarms, irregular barbarian raids and attack size scaling.
vc.configuration.category.other.tooltip: Additional settings that do not yet have a dedicated section.
vc.configuration.maxCitizens.tooltip: Hard citizen cap per town, even after population upgrades. Housing beds are also required. Default: 64.
vc.configuration.basePopulation.tooltip: Citizen limit before a town buys population upgrades. The town still needs enough housing beds. Default: 10.
vc.configuration.populationPerUpgrade.to: How many additional citizens each population upgrade allows, up to Maximum population. Default: 5.
vc.configuration.populationUpgradeCost.t: Emerald price of the first population upgrade. Each later upgrade adds this price again: a value of 8 means costs of 8, 16, 24, and so on.
vc.configuration.stationUpgradeCost.tool: Emerald price of the first station range or crew upgrade. Each further level doubles the price: a value of 8 means costs of 8, 16 and 32.
vc.configuration.quarryWorkers.tooltip: Starting workers per Quarry Station, before crew upgrades. Default: 8.
vc.configuration.enchantMinutes.tooltip: Base minutes per book or common item. Iron and gold gear take 1.3 times as long, diamond 1.6 times, and netherite twice as long. Rarer items also take longer. Default: 5 minutes.
vc.configuration.enchanterMaxLevel.toolt: Highest enchanting-table level an enchanter can reach, regardless of bookshelves. This is the table level, not the enchantment numeral on an item. Default: 25; level 30 remains for players.
vc.configuration.oreVeinSeconds.tooltip: Each ore block has its own saved replenishment delay. Miners rotate between ready ores. Better pickaxes shorten the delay, capped at 1.5 times stone speed. Gold ore takes twice as long, diamond and emerald six times, ancient debris eight.
vc.configuration.mineMinY.tooltip: Lowest floor Y a new tunnel mine can randomly choose. Default: -30. Existing mine plans keep their saved depth.
vc.configuration.mineMaxY.tooltip: Highest floor Y a new tunnel mine can randomly choose. Default: 10. Existing mine plans keep their saved depth.
vc.configuration.quarryTargetY.tooltip: Bottom Y for a newly created quarry plan. Bedrock is preserved. Default: -64. Existing quarry plans keep their saved target.
vc.configuration.mineBranchLength.toolti: Length of each strip-mine side tunnel, in blocks. Default: 24. Applies when a new mine plan is created.
vc.configuration.mineBranchPairs.tooltip: Number of paired side tunnels along the mine spine, spaced three blocks apart. Default: 4 pairs, or 8 side tunnels. Applies to new mine plans.
vc.configuration.workTicks.tooltip: Working ticks needed to harvest a block after reaching it. Lower values make harvesting faster. At the normal tick rate, 20 ticks = 1 second; the default 80 ticks = 4 seconds.
vc.configuration.rationTicks.tooltip: Loaded ticks between meals before applying the multiplier. 20 ticks = 1 second. Default base 2400, multiplied by 3, gives one regular meal every 6 minutes. Healing meals have a 30-second cooldown.
vc.configuration.alarmThreshold.tooltip: Number of hostiles citizens must sight at once before a guard runs to ring the town bell. Individual threats can still call guards without a town-wide alarm. Default: 10.
vc.configuration.enemyWaves.tooltip: Enable automatic barbarian raids while a settlement manager is home. Turning this off stops scheduled raids; ordinary monsters still exist.
vc.configuration.waveMinPopulation.toolt: Minimum citizen population before automatic waves are scheduled. Default: 3 citizens.
vc.configuration.waveIntervalDays.toolti: Average Minecraft days between raids, with up to 40 percent variation either way. Arrival waits for sunset and a manager at home. Default: 5 days, giving 3-7 days before the next eligible night. Saved overrides remain in force.
vc.configuration.waveBaseMobs.tooltip: Barbarians in a raid before citizen and population-upgrade scaling. Default: 1.
vc.configuration.waveMobsPerCitizen.tool: Additional barbarians per citizen, rounded up. Default: 0.35, or about one extra raider per three citizens.
vc.configuration.waveMaxMobs.tooltip: Raid size cap before population upgrades. Default: 32. Upgrades can add raiders beyond this cap.
vc.configuration.waveMobsPerUpgrade.tool: Extra raiders per population upgrade, also above the base cap. First two raids: foot soldiers; from raid three: archers; from raid six in developed towns: armored veterans. Default: 2.
vc.configuration.maxActiveTraders.toolti: Maximum towns with an active trader chunk window in this dimension. Each uses a moving 3x3 area (9 chunks), rather than loading the entire route. Default: 8. Extra traders wait.
vc.configuration.tradeRouteDistance.tool: Maximum distance between town banners for a trader route. Routes need walkable terrain or roads and remain in the Overworld. Default: 8192 blocks.
vc.configuration.ensureNearbyNpcTown.too: Establish a nearby NPC neighbour on safe terrain when none is available. Temporarily holds one 3x3 chunk window, then releases it. Respects random settlements, town limits and existing claims.
vc.configuration.randomSettlements.toolt: Discover small working NPC towns in suitable loaded Overworld terrain. Existing NPC towns remain when this is disabled. They begin neutral, produce real goods, and can accept supply routes.
vc.configuration.npcTownGrowth.tooltip: The shared NPC director manages food priorities, material-funded buildings and food-funded immigration. Decisions are saved; building pauses near players and never loads terrain.
vc.configuration.npcGrowthDays.tooltip: Minecraft days between building projects and immigration attempts. Default: 1 day. No bulk catch-up after a long absence.
vc.configuration.npcExtraBuildings.toolt: Maximum buildings added to each NPC town. Default: 4, including cottages, a workshop and an inn. Projects use real stock and safe space inside the existing claim.
vc.configuration.npcHighways.tooltip: Build shared dirt highways between agreed trading towns in surveyed, already loaded land. Construction does not force or generate chunks, change player claims, or spend player stock. Both NPC and player traders can use the saved network.
vc.configuration.pregeneratedRoads.toolt: Lay dirt roads between native town sites while new terrain generates near the world centre. Towns on these roads trade along them. Farther out, towns build their own roads as they trade, so the network keeps growing the longer the world runs.
How far pregenerated roads reach from the world centre along each axis. Default: 5000, the first 10,000 x 10,000 blocks. Zero disables them. Only affects terrain generated after the change.
vc.configuration.npcConstructionDistance: Closest a player may be while an NPC building or new highway is constructed. Default: 96 blocks; work resumes after the player leaves.
vc.configuration.npcTownSpacing.tooltip: Region size used to space candidate towns. Default: 1408 blocks, usually about 1000–2000 blocks between nearby candidates. Terrain and player claims can leave larger gaps. Changing this affects future discoveries.
vc.configuration.maxNpcTowns.tooltip: Maximum automatically generated NPC towns in the Overworld. Default: 48; zero prevents new discoveries. This does not remove existing towns.
vc.configuration.category.world.tooltip: Trader travel limits and discovery of neutral NPC settlements.
Multiplies the base meal interval, including saved settings in existing worlds. Default: 3. The default 2400-tick base becomes 7200 loaded ticks (6 minutes).
vc.configuration.fishingSeconds.tooltip: Time fishing at a dry bank beside open, two-block-deep water. Default: 30 seconds per whole fish. Butchers prepare catches before cooks can use them.
vc.configuration.animalBreeders.tooltip: Adult animals preserved in each keeper pen per species. Default: 4. Keepers use real feed and harvest surplus adults. Babies, named animals and mating animals are preserved.
vc.configuration.expeditionSites.tooltip: Discover finite camps, occupied mines and ruined forts in unclaimed natural terrain.
vc.configuration.maxExpeditionSites.tool: Keep this many discovered sites, including cleared sites and outposts.
vc.configuration.maxExpeditionBandits.to: Cap living expedition defenders and convoy raiders, including unloaded defenders.
vc.configuration.convoyRaids.tooltip: Nearby occupied camps can warn of and launch raids while players are nearby.
vc.configuration.yieldUpgradeCost.toolti: First farm or mine yield upgrade price. Each level doubles it: 16, 32 and 64 emeralds by default, for 10%, 20% and 30% average extra produce or mineral drops.
vc.configuration.category.diagnostics.to: Server logs for sustained worker problems and citizen recovery.
vc.configuration.serverDiagnostics.toolt: Write worker and recovery diagnostics to the server console and latest.log. Default: enabled. Recipe exceptions always log their ID and stack trace.
Loaded seconds of a sustained worker problem before its first warning. Default: 120; range: 10 to 3600. Ordinary idle work and off-duty citizens are excluded.
vc.configuration.diagnosticRepeatSeconds: Minimum seconds between repeat warnings of the same kind for one citizen. Default: 300; range: 30 to 3600. Changing activity or job does not bypass the worker-warning cooldown.
tooltip.vc.raw_tin: Smelt raw tin in a furnace to make Tin Ingots.
tooltip.vc.tin_ingot: Mix 1 Tin Ingot with 3 Copper Ingots to make 4 Bronze Blends.
tooltip.vc.bronze_blend.craft: Legacy blend: already-made blends can still be smelted.
tooltip.vc.bronze_blend.smelt: New bronze comes directly from an Alloy Furnace: 3 copper + 1 tin + separate fuel.
tooltip.vc.bronze_blend.research: Alloy furnaces need Bronze Age research in their settlement.
vc.configuration.maxSettlementTraps.tool: Maximum placed traps per town. Only traps in ticking chunks activate; each activation spends durability.
tooltip.vc.research_scroll: Written by researchers at lecterns. Spend at your town banner or trade with another settlement.
vc.configuration.startingClaimRadius.too: Starting radius for new towns. Default: 120 blocks (241 x 241), half the old radius. Buy further land at the banner under More. Saved claims retain their radius.
Radius added by each paid border expansion. Default: 32 blocks per edge, capped at radius 512. Expansion cannot overlap another town.
vc.configuration.borderUpgradeCost.toolt: Emerald price of the first border expansion. Default: 16; later prices are 32, 48, 64 and so on.
vc.configuration.initialNpcTowns.tooltip: Place furnished towns as Minecraft structures while new chunks generate. Enable Generate Structures.
vc.configuration.npcFoundingDelayDays.to: Elapsed Minecraft days before new towns may emerge in loaded terrain. Sleeping does not skip this delay.
